## Overview

10x Genomics 3' chemistries capture the 3' end of transcripts. In non-model genomes the gene models usually have short or missing 3' UTRs, so many reads land just downstream of the annotated gene and are thrown away. [GeneExt](https://github.com/sebepedroslab/GeneExt) uses the reads themselves to extend gene models at the 3' end. More reads are then assigned to genes, giving more UMIs and genes per cell. (Background and first tests: [GeneExt on scRNA-seq data](../notebook/2024-09-10-geneextend-on-scrnaseq-data.md).)

The pipeline runs Cell Ranger twice: once with the original annotation (only to get BAMs for GeneExt), and once with the extended annotation (the counts you analyze). CellBender then removes ambient RNA.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  F[FASTQs<br/>per library] --> C1[1. cellranger count<br/>original ref]
  C1 --> M[2. samtools merge<br/>all BAMs]
  M --> G[3. GeneExt<br/>extend 3' ends]
  G --> R[4. cellranger mkref<br/>extended GTF]
  R --> C2[5. cellranger count<br/>extended ref]
  F --> C2
  C2 --> B[6. CellBender<br/>ambient RNA]
  B --> O[(filtered .h5<br/>for Seurat / scanpy)]
```

Every step is submitted as an LSF job that waits (`#BSUB -w "done(...)"`) on the step before it. You submit the whole chain once and get an email as each job finishes.

## Inputs

All of these go in your config file (see [Run it](#run-it)).

| Input | Config setting | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Genome FASTA | `FASTA` | |
| Gene models (GTF) | `GTF` | Exon-only, validated GTF. Cell Ranger and GeneExt both need consistent `gene_id`/`transcript_id` attributes. |
| Cell Ranger reference built from the original GTF | `REF_ORIG` | Reuse one if it exists; otherwise set `RUN_MKREF_ORIG=true` and the pipeline builds it. |
| FASTQ folder per library | `LIB_FASTQS` | One folder per library |
| FASTQ sample prefix per library | `LIB_SAMPLES` | The start of the FASTQ file names, passed to `cellranger count --sample` |
| Library IDs | `LIB_IDS` | Short names used for output folders, e.g. `lib-001` |

## Software

| Tool | How it's loaded (defaults in the config; change them for your cluster) |
|---|---|
| Cell Ranger 8.0.0 | `module load cellranger/8.0.0` |
| samtools | conda env `samtools_env` (keep it up to date, see [Known issues](#known-issues)) |
| GeneExt | git clone of [GeneExt](https://github.com/sebepedroslab/GeneExt) (`GENEEXT_INSTALL`) + conda env `geneext` ([install notes](../notebook/2024-09-10-geneextend-on-scrnaseq-data.md)) |
| CellBender | conda env `CellBender` |

How the conda environments were set up on the University of Miami Pegasus cluster: [Pegasus conda environments](../notebook/2024-10-30-pegasus-conda-environments.md).

Default resources for every step: queue `bigmem`, 16 cores, `rusage[mem=15000]`, 24–120 h walltime. Change `QUEUE`, `CORES` and `MEM_MB` in the config for your cluster.

## Run it {#run-it}

The script never needs editing. Everything specific to your run (paths, library names, email, LSF project) goes in a small config file.

1. **Make a config file** on the cluster login node:

   ```bash
   bash scrnaseq_10x_geneext_cellbender.sh --init my_run.config
   ```

2. **Fill it in.** Open `my_run.config` (`nano my_run.config`) and replace every `<fill in: ...>` value. Use absolute paths. Software settings (module names, conda env names) have defaults you can change.

   ```bash
   RUN="<fill in: short run name, used in job and reference names, e.g. species_runID>"
   EMAIL="<fill in: email for LSF job notifications>"
   FASTA="<fill in: /path/to/genome.fa>"
   LIB_IDS=(     "<fill in: library ID 1, e.g. lib-001>"     "<fill in: library ID 2>" )
   # ...
   ```

3. **Submit the chain:**

   ```bash
   bash scrnaseq_10x_geneext_cellbender.sh my_run.config
   bjobs -w | grep <your RUN name>        # check progress
   ```

   Before submitting anything, the script stops if any `<fill in>` value is left, if the library lists have different lengths, or if the FASTA, GTF, reference, FASTQ folders or GeneExt install can't be found.

4. **If a step fails**, fix the problem, `bkill` the jobs still waiting, and resume from that step. Earlier outputs are reused:

   ```bash
   START_AT=3 bash scrnaseq_10x_geneext_cellbender.sh my_run.config   # 2 = merge, 3 = GeneExt, 5 = second count, 6 = CellBender
   ```

The exact job file for every step is saved in `<OUTDIR>/logs/` next to its `.out`/`.err` logs, so each run keeps a record of what was submitted. Keep the config file with your project notes: it is the full record of a run's settings.

## Outputs

For each library `<lib>`, in `${OUTDIR}/<lib>_geneext/`:

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `outs/web_summary.html` | Cell Ranger QC report (compare with the step-1 report in `${OUTDIR}/<lib>/outs/`) |
| `<lib>_geneext_cellbender_output_filtered.h5` | **The matrix to analyze**: CellBender-corrected, cell barcodes only |
| `<lib>_geneext_cellbender_output_metrics.csv` | CellBender summary metrics |
| `<lib>_geneext_cellbender_output_report.html` / `.pdf` | CellBender training and QC report |

Plus `${OUTDIR}/<run>_GeneExt.gtf` (the extended annotation), with `.extension_length.pdf` and `.peak_coverage.pdf` plots from GeneExt.

Copy them back to your laptop:

```bash
H=<fill in: user@cluster.address>
D=<fill in: OUTDIR from your config>
for lib in <fill in: your LIB_IDS, space-separated>; do
  scp $H:$D/${lib}/outs/web_summary.html            ./${lib}_web_summary.html
  scp $H:$D/${lib}_geneext/outs/web_summary.html    ./${lib}_web_summary_geneext.html
  for f in .pdf _filtered.h5 _metrics.csv _report.html; do
    scp $H:$D/${lib}_geneext/${lib}_geneext_cellbender_output${f} ./
  done
done
```

## Known issues {#known-issues}

::: {.callout-warning collapse="false"}
## GeneExt must run from its install directory, with no old `tmp/`
GeneExt writes intermediate files to `./tmp` and calls its plotting scripts with relative paths (`Rscript geneext/plot_extensions.R …`). Run it from anywhere else and those steps fail. A `tmp/` left over from a crashed run also breaks the next run. The script `cd`s into `GENEEXT_INSTALL` and runs `rm -rf tmp` first. Because of the shared `tmp/`, **don't run two GeneExt jobs at the same time** from the same install.
:::

::: {.callout-warning collapse="false"}
## `samtools merge` failed with the old samtools in `samtools_env`
The first full run ([Pdam 31298](../notebook/2026-05-07-pdam-31298-cellranger-geneext-cellbender-run.md)) failed at the merge step. Updating samtools in the environment fixed it. The job now prints `samtools --version` and runs `samtools quickcheck` on the merged BAM, so a bad merge stops the chain before GeneExt.
<!-- TODO: paste the exact error message here so it shows up in search -->
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## A failed step leaves the rest of the chain stuck in `PEND`
LSF never satisfies `done(<jobid>)` for a job that exited with an error, so the downstream jobs wait forever. Check with `bjobs -l <jobid>` ("dependency condition invalid or never satisfied"), `bkill` them, fix the problem, and resubmit with `START_AT=<step>`.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Checking BAMs: use samtools, not `wc -l`
BAMs are compressed binary files, so `wc -l` doesn't count reads. Use `samtools quickcheck file.bam` (is the file intact?) or `samtools view -c file.bam` (how many reads?).
:::

## Example run

- [Pdam 31298 (all cells + ALDH+), May 2026](../notebook/2026-05-07-pdam-31298-cellranger-geneext-cellbender-run.md). GeneExt extended **13,283 / 25,422** genes, median extension **1,297 bp**.
